summary.short: Sets privacy and confidentiality rules for public electronic communications in the UK from 11 December 2003: consent for storing information on terminal equipment, traffic and location data limits, calling line identification, directories, unsolicited direct marketing by calls, fax and email, breach notification and security duties for communications providers.
summary.long: These Regulations, made under the European Communities Act 1972 to implement parts of Directive 2002/58/EC, come into force on 11 December 2003 and revoke the Telecommunications (Data Protection and Privacy) Regulations 1999. Providers of public electronic communications services must take appropriate security measures (reg. 5), notify personal data breaches to the Information Commission and, where likely to adversely affect a subscriber or user, to that subscriber or user (reg. 5A). Regulation 6 prohibits storing information in, or accessing information in, a subscriber's or user's terminal equipment unless an exception in Schedule A1 applies, including consent. Regulations 7 and 8 restrict the processing of traffic data, and regulation 14 restricts location data. Regulations 10 to 13 require calling and connected line identification facilities, and regulation 15 to 16A cover malicious calls, emergency calls and emergency alerts. Regulation 18 governs directories of subscribers, and regulation 19 to 24 restrict direct marketing by automated calling systems, fax, calls and email, subject to consent, opt-out and register rules. Regulations 25 and 26 require the Information Commission to keep registers of numbers. Regulation 27 voids inconsistent contract terms, and regulations 28 and 29 exempt national security and legal-requirement cases. Regulation 30 allows damages claims, and regulation 31 and Schedule 1 apply Data Protection Act 2018 enforcement powers, including a fixed monetary penalty of £1,000 for breach-notification failures (reg. 5C). Regulations 32A to 32C provide for codes of conduct and accreditation of monitoring bodies, and regulation 37 requires periodic reviews by the Secretary of State.</think>
